name: Lemon-Garlic Steak Bites with Tallow Potatoes & Green Beans
ingredients:
1.5 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, cut in 1-inch chunks
1/2 tsp baking soda
1 tbsp beef tallow
1.25 lb top sirloin, trimmed, cut in 1-inch cubes
1 lb green beans, trimmed
5 garlic cloves, minced
1 lemon, zested and juiced
1 tbsp avocado oil, divided
1.5 tsp salt, plus more for the potato water
3/4 tsp black pepper
directions:
Parboil potatoes: Place potatoes in a pot of cold, well-salted water with the baking soda. Bring to a boil and cook 6–8 minutes, until a knife slides in but they hold their shape.
Season beef: While the potatoes boil, pat the sirloin dry and season with half the salt and all the pepper.
Drain and rough up: Drain the potatoes and let them steam-dry for 2 minutes. Shake the colander hard to rough up the edges.
Crisp potatoes: Heat the tallow in a cast-iron skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Add potatoes in one layer and leave untouched 4–5 minutes, until deep golden underneath and they release on their own. Flip and repeat, about 12–15 minutes total. Keep them going while you cook the beans and beef.
Blister green beans: In a second large skillet over medium-high, add half the avocado oil, the green beans, and a pinch of salt. Toss occasionally until blistered and crisp-tender, about 6 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Sear beef: Turn the second skillet to high. Add the remaining avocado oil and the beef in a single layer. Sear 1–2 minutes per side until browned outside and pink inside.
Garlic and lemon: Lower the heat, add most of the garlic, and stir 30 seconds. Return the beans, add the lemon juice and most of the zest, and toss.
Finish potatoes and serve: Toss the potatoes with the remaining salt, garlic, and lemon zest for the last 30 seconds. Serve alongside the steak and beans.
notes:
Roughly 32g protein and 12g fat per serving.
The baking soda breaks down the potato surfaces; roughed-up, fuzzy edges are what turn into the crunchy crust. Parboiled potatoes are soft, so handle gently and don't flip until they release.
Pat the beef dry for a real sear, and never crowd either pan.
Flank steak works in place of sirloin.
